items.followUp: Draw and label a chloroplast, showing its membranes, grana and stroma.

rubric.why: Identifies the chloroplast’s double boundary.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the chloroplast is bounded by an outer and an inner membrane.

rubric.why: Names the fluid interior of the chloroplast.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the stroma as the fluid-filled space inside the inner membrane.

rubric.why: Identifies the stacked membrane sacs within the chloroplast.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that grana are stacks of thylakoids.

rubric.why: Includes the connecting membranes between grana.
rubric.how: Award for identifying intergranal lamellae as connections between grana.

rubric.why: A labelled diagram demonstrates the main structure.
rubric.how: Award for a chloroplast sketch labelled with chloroplast, grana and stroma; the double membrane should also be shown.

modelAnswer: A chloroplast is surrounded by an outer and an inner membrane.
The interior contains a fluid called stroma.
Within the stroma are flattened membrane sacs called thylakoids, arranged in stacks called grana.
Grana are connected to one another by intergranal lamellae.
Diagram: draw an oval chloroplast with a double outline; show several stacks of discs (grana) inside, connected by lamellae, and label the outer membrane, inner membrane, stroma, granum and lamellae.

items.followUp: State two reasons why a standard system of naming organisms is useful.

rubric.why: Explains that scientific names are used internationally.
rubric.how: Award for stating that binomial names are accepted and used worldwide.

rubric.why: Recognises that common names vary and can cause ambiguity.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that scientific names avoid confusion caused by different local or common names.

rubric.why: Describes the two-part naming system.
rubric.how: Award for stating that each scientific name has two parts: genus and species.

rubric.why: Notes that the name gives information useful for classification or relationships.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the genus name can indicate an organism’s group or relationship to similar organisms.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature gives every species a universally accepted scientific name.
It avoids confusion because common names may differ between languages and regions.
Each scientific name consists of two words: the genus name followed by the species name.
The genus name also helps show an organism’s classification and relationship to similar organisms.

items.followUp: Define a balanced diet and name two nutrients that provide energy.

rubric.why: Defines dietary fibre as the indigestible part of plant food, also called roughage.
rubric.how: Award for describing fibre as indigestible plant material or roughage.

rubric.why: Names the two types of dietary fibre.
rubric.how: Award for naming both soluble and insoluble fibre.

rubric.why: Gives examples of fibre types or components.
rubric.how: Award for giving a suitable example, such as cellulose for insoluble fibre or pectin for soluble fibre.

rubric.why: Explains how fibre supports bowel movement and digestive health.
rubric.how: Award for stating that fibre adds bulk to faeces and/or promotes peristalsis, helping prevent constipation.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibre, or roughage, is the indigestible part of plant food.
Its two types are soluble fibre, such as pectin, and insoluble fibre, such as cellulose.
Fibre adds bulk to faeces and helps food move through the intestine by peristalsis.
It helps maintain regular bowel movements and prevents constipation.

items.followUp: Compare the structures and functions of arteries and capillaries.

rubric.why: States the direction in which arteries carry blood.
rubric.description: Arteries carry blood away from the heart
rubric.how: Award for stating that arteries carry blood away from the heart.

rubric.why: States the direction in which veins carry blood.
rubric.description: Veins carry blood towards the heart
rubric.how: Award for stating that veins carry blood towards the heart.

rubric.why: Compares the strong artery wall with the thinner vein wall.
rubric.how: Award for describing artery walls as thick, muscular and elastic, in contrast to thinner, less elastic vein walls.

rubric.why: Compares the internal space of the vessels.
rubric.how: Award for stating that arteries have a narrower lumen and veins a wider lumen.

rubric.why: Includes a further structural or functional contrast.
rubric.how: Award for noting that veins have valves (arteries generally do not) or that blood flows at higher pressure in arteries than in veins.

modelAnswer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood towards the heart.
Arteries have thick, muscular, elastic walls; veins have thinner, less elastic walls.
Arteries have a narrower lumen; veins have a wider lumen.
Veins contain valves to prevent the backflow of blood; arteries generally do not have valves.
Blood flows through arteries at higher pressure, while blood in veins is at lower pressure.

items.followUp: Define zoology and name the branch of biology that studies plants.

rubric.why: Gives the standard definition of biology.
rubric.how: Award both marks for defining biology as the science or study of life or living organisms.

modelAnswer: Biology is the science that deals with the study of life and living organisms.

rubric.why: Identifies the zone of life as the part or region of Earth where organisms live.
rubric.how: Award for describing the zone of life as the region or part of Earth in which life exists.

rubric.why: Identifies the major parts of Earth included in the zone of life.
rubric.description: Components of the zone of life
rubric.how: Award for naming land, water and air, or the lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere.

modelAnswer: The zone of life, or biosphere, is the region of Earth where living organisms exist.
It includes parts of the land, water and air.

items.followUp: Write the scientific names of wheat and the housefly.

rubric.why: Gives the scientific name of mustard.
rubric.how: Award for the binomial name Brassica campestris.

rubric.why: Gives the scientific name of the frog used in the textbook.
rubric.how: Award for the binomial name Rana tigrina.

modelAnswer: Mustard plant: Brassica campestris.
Frog: Rana tigrina.

rubric.why: Identifies a biological problem as a question or problem concerning living organisms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is a question or problem related to living organisms.

rubric.why: States that the problem is investigated or solved scientifically.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it can be investigated or solved by the scientific or biological method.

modelAnswer: A biological problem is a question or problem about living organisms.
It is investigated and solved by using the biological method.
